citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
As documented in a June 1, 2026 noncompliance letter from the facility to USDA Animal Care, along with a disposition
record and the May 22, 2026 IACUC noncompliance meeting minutes, a significant deviation from the approved IACUC
study protocol was identified. It was reported that a disabled, non releasable female adult black vulture was released back
into the wild following the conclusion of the study. The principal investigator (PI) released the animal into the wild on
March 5, 2026 and subsequently closed the protocol on March 13, 2026. The IACUC noncompliance meeting minutes
further note that the PI acknowledged releasing the black vulture associated with Protocol #25-274. Because the
approved protocol did not authorize release of the animal, this acknowledgment confirmed that an activity occurred
outside the scope of the approved protocol. Within the Protocol #25-274 document, “Recovered Black Vulture for
Teaching and Research,” multiple sections explain that the bird was originally found with a broken wing, required wing
amputation, could not be released, and would be permanently maintained in captivity for teaching purposes. On July 27,
2026 the vulture was recaptured by the facility and now resides at a wildlife rehabilitation center.
This activity constitutes a significant deviation from the approved protocol. Implementing substantial changes to protocols,
such as releasing a bird missing part of its wing into the wild, without prior IACUC review and approval deprives the
IACUC of its ability to provide appropriate oversight of animal activities and ensure compliance with the Animal Welfare
Act. Failure to allow the IACUC to conduct an review of the IACUC protocol may result in serious adverse impacts on
animal welfare. Per this section of the regulations, the IACUC must review and approve significant changes to proposals
for animal use before the investigators can conduct any additional activities that were not initially described at the time of
IACUC approval. Corrected prior to the time of inspection.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
The facility did not follow the Program of Veterinary Care (PVC) as required. The physical exam record for canine USDA
#3800 dated November 25, 2025 documented abnormal findings including gingivitis and moderate dental calculi. The
medical record indicates that the last dental prophylaxis was performed on January 14, 2025. Under Section IV C of the
‑
PVC, preventative care requires maintaining clean and healthy teeth, stating that “dental prophylaxis must be performed
annually or more frequently if needed.” The PVC outlines appropriate methods to prevent, control, diagnose, and treat
diseases and injuries. When the PVC is not properly followed, expected medical outcomes may not occur, existing
conditions may worsen, or new issues may arise. Correct by September 28, 2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with the attending veterinarian and a facility representative.
